Hi Sophie — thanks, and glad the demo was useful. Attaching a draft MAP and a concise benchmarking plan (PDF). High level plan below; the attachment has the detailed test matrix and gating criteria.

Summary of the proposed MAP (high level)
- Week 0 (2027-05-03): Agreement on targets and test windows; DocuSign amendment prep.
- Week 1 (2027-05-10 to 2027-05-12): Pilot test run (burst + steady-state).
- Week 2 (2027-05-17): Analysis, recommended rate-limit tuning, and final SLO proposal; follow-up meeting.

Benchmarking approach (what we will measure)
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 measured at token-level and end-to-end request time. TTFT (time-to-first-token) captured separately for cold and warmed KV-cache.
- Throughput: sustained qps during steady-state windows; max sustainable throughput and failure rates.
- Concurrency experiments: ramped concurrency to evaluate queueing behavior, headroom, and tail latency impact. We will run controlled bursts (10s/60s/300s windows) and sustained steady-state runs (30min).
- Queueing & backpressure: observe queue length, queuing delay, reject rates; measure recovery time after a burst.
- Rate-limit tuning: we’ll test two configurations during the pilot and recommend a tuned policy (token-bucket style limits + quick-fallback).

Gates for success (examples)
- No P95 regression > 20% vs baseline under steady-state at 500 qps.
- TTFT < 500ms for cold path in > 90% of requests.
- Sustained error rate < 0.5% at target throughput.

Attachments: 2027-05-01_MAP-proposal.pdf (detailed test matrix, resource owners, and sample Gatling jobs).

If that looks good I'll loop in Neha and Rishi for test setup and scheduling. Do you want Redwood to run the load from our dedicated pool in us-west-2 or do you prefer to run from your cloud account?

— Logan

Subject: RE: MAP: performance benchmarking + stress-window test plan (Acme.ai) — results summary

Sophie — quick summary from the pilot run this week (artifacts attached: stresswindow-gatling-logs.tar.gz, map-stresswindow-results.csv). Full deck will follow.

Executive summary (top-line)
- Steady-state (500 qps sustained, 30m): P50 = 38ms, P95 = 210ms, error rate = 0.12%. TTFT (warmed cache) median = 42ms. Gate: PASSED.
- Burst runs: 15k concurrent target produced a sharp queueing onset at ~9.5k concurrent; during 60s bursts we saw P95 spike to 1.4s and a 1.1% retry rate. For 10s micro-bursts, the system absorbed up to 11k with acceptable degradation (P95 ~420ms).
- Recovery: average time to return to steady-state after a 300s burst was ~90s.

Rate-limit tuning recommendations
- Default policy during pilot: token-bucket at 200 rps per tenant, global small-burst allowance (burst = 2x token rate for 20s).
- Recommended tuned policy for Acme: reduce default burst allowance (to 1.5x) and set a soft-queue threshold at 8k concurrent, with an automatic ramp-down (graceful reject) rather than abrupt hard rejects. This improved P95 tail behavior in our follow-up runs.

Action items
- Redwood: produce final MAP results deck + short executive summary for procurement (ETA 2027-05-11).
- Redwood Ops (Neha): share raw logs and dashboards (Drive link in related links).
- Acme: confirm if you want Redwood to include the SLO-credit clause in DocuSign; Sophie to share procurement template.

Attachments: map-stresswindow-results.csv (summary metrics), stresswindow-gatling-logs.tar.gz (raw load generator logs).

Thanks — Logan
